14675-secret-enemies-of-true-republicani:
Andrew B. Smolnikar, once a monk, priest, and teacher of Bible books, wrote this long tract on the secret foes of true republicanism and the age of peace to come. The text was cleaned of many plain typos.

Smolnikar says signs and dreams made him a voice for a world republic, and he urges Ohio's leaders and workers to end wars and revolts. His pages call for truth and peace among all men, and for rule built on good will rather than force. The tract mixes faith, foretelling, and politics. It is a strange piece of old-time writing on the end times, earnest and odd, and it shows how one man's hopes for peace took the shape of a holy cause.
8605-unitarianism-in-america-a-history-o:
George Willis Cooke traces Unitarianism in the United States from its obscure beginnings in New England to an organized denomination with a record of achievement. His preface admits that limits of space keep the earliest phase cursory, but promises a fuller account than earlier writers gave of how the movement formed, organized itself, and grew. Cooke writes as a historian and a member of several learned societies.

The history follows ministers, churches, controversies, and institutions, showing how a liberal theology took shape in a country still shaped by Calvinism. Readers interested in American religion will find a clear institutional narrative, less concerned with doctrine than with people and organization. The book remains a standard early history of the movement, valuable for its scope even where later scholarship has revised its judgments.
doe-osti-17014403-ocp-logbook-09-08-2026: Single shift logbook entry by En-Chuan Huang of Los Alamos National Laboratory records nES beam development work on September 8, 2026. Huang and Brad on the physics team finished tuning the WNR beam line, though the slow controls maxed out one unit, and they chose to minimize a setting named 1RAP4 instead. Notes cover software versions in use, a choice between upstream and downstream data, a long run numbered 192135, and a leave taking checklist for quads, permits, and closed software. Screenshot attachments from the tuning tool close the short record.
secret-enemies-of-true-republicanism-mos:
Andrew B. Smolnikar published this long treatise at Springhill, Pennsylvania, in 1859. Smolnikar had spent eighteen years as a Benedictine monk and a crown professor of Bible studies before leaving that life in 1838. He held that signs and forecasts had named him a herald of a new age.

Smolnikar argues that hidden foes block true republican rule and stir up wars and revolts. His plan would free nations from kings and harsh rule, then bring lasting peace and fairness to the whole globe. The book blends faith, forecasts, and politics in a call for a world remade.
unitarianism-in-america-a-history-of-its:
George Willis Cooke wrote Unitarianism in America to trace where the movement began in the United States, how it organized itself, and what it achieved. In his preface he says the obscure New England beginnings deserved fuller treatment than they had yet received, though his space forced him to keep that part brief. He likewise touches only lightly on the church fights that split the Unitarians from the older Congregational body.

Cooke names the writers he means to supplement rather than replace. They include George E. Ellis on the half century of controversy, Joseph Henry Allen on the liberal movement, William Channing Gannett's memoir of Ezra Stiles Gannett, and John White Chadwick on old and new beliefs. Readers get a survey built to fill gaps in those earlier works, with stress on institutions and growth rather than on doctrine alone.
